statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NQ extended its decline to a fourth consecutive lower low at 31,144.50 and trades near 31,216.75, down 0.85%, but roughly 72 points of retracement off that low keeps Tail at 23 inside the watch band. VIX at 15.85 below its session high and both the 10-year and 30-year yields paring off 24-year highs leave the amplifier stack incomplete, while a 1.20% range and Brent above $101 hold Stress elevated into the 18:00Z FOMC minutes.
recommendation: Tail remains in the watch band and below the block threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans the 17:00Z 10-year note auction, the 18:00Z September FOMC minutes and the hours of possible delayed yield-led repricing into the 20:00Z cash close, where the published forecast reaches the elevated band for three slots.
headline: NQ sets a fourth consecutive lower low at 31,144.50 but retraces about 72 points off it, holding Tail at 23 while 24-year-high yields pare back and VIX stays at 15.85 into the FOMC minutes
body:
NQ December futures trade near 31,216.75, down 266.50 points or 0.85%, against a 31,483.25 previous close and an open at 31,510.00. The session range is 31,144.50 to 31,521.00, about 376 points or 1.20%. Two independent quote sources agree within thirteen points on price and within two points on the session low, with the freshest tick timed 14:16Z. The material change from the previous hour is that the 31,209.75 low published then has been taken out by roughly 65 points, making this a fourth consecutive hour of lower lows, and the U.S. cash session opened lower and extended the move. Set against that, price now sits about 72 points above the new extreme, the widest retracement off a session low so far today, against roughly 47 points an hour ago. A widening bounce off the extreme is the opposite of the shallow-pullback signature that defines a pathological path, so Tail steps only to 23 and stays in the watch band short of the block threshold.

The amplifier stack has partly decayed rather than completed. Aligned against mean reversion: the lower-low sequence has now persisted four hours, the cash open continued the decline from the record highs set on 6 October, Brent is above $101.82 and WTI near $89.94 on Houthi attacks against Saudi infrastructure, at least nine attacks in the Strait of Hormuz this month and a Gulf Coast tropical storm that has prompted Chevron to evacuate offshore personnel, and the FOMC minutes at 18:00Z are a credible unresolved multi-stage mechanism given Chair Warsh's hawkish September stance after the 25 basis point hike to 3.75-4.00%.

Against that, three independent amplifiers that would normally be required for Tail at or above 25 are absent. VIX is 15.85, up 5.6% but below its 16.01 session high and low in absolute terms for a session of this description. The 10-year yield touched 5.36%, its highest since April 2002, and has pared to 5.32%, the bottom of its day range; the 30-year touched 5.73%, its highest since May 2002, and has pared to 5.70%, also the bottom of its range, against the 5.31% and 5.66% recorded for 5 October in the Federal Reserve H.15 release. A yield amplifier that is easing off its highs, not extending, materially weakens the yield-led transmission case for this hour. Index dispersion is also orderly: the Dow opened down 0.8%, the Nasdaq 0.7% and the S&P 500 0.5%, which is a broad pullback from a record rather than a technology-specific breakdown, and Nvidia at $237.84 is only marginally lower.

Stress rises to 54 on the wider 1.20% range, the firmer VIX, the standing 24-year-high yield backdrop, Brent above $100 and the event stack still ahead. That is an elevated and difficult environment that can still mean-revert, and it is deliberately not allowed to drive the current action. Confidence holds at 87 on two agreeing live quote sources, live VIX and live 10-year and 30-year yields with intraday ranges, the official H.15 release, current crude prices, a verified U.S. calendar and verified September FOMC context; the shared Finviz context file was unavailable for use this hour, reported partial collection and carried an eight-day-old collection timestamp, so it was discarded and played no part in this assessment.

The published forecast therefore keeps the current hour in the watch band, firms into the 15:00Z inflation-expectations print, and reaches the elevated band for the 17:00Z auction and the two hours covering the FOMC minutes and the delayed-second-leg window, before decaying through the cash close into an overnight baseline. Before those events print, hypothetical post-release alignment is treated as conditional and not as observed structure.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours of published Claude assessments held the mapped EA_ON state apart from five WATCH hours: 15:00Z and 16:00Z on 6 October, when Tail reached 22 and 20 during the U.S. cash session, and 11:00Z, 12:00Z and 13:00Z today, when Tail stepped to 21, 21 and 22. Tail decayed from the high teens to a flat 10 through the 6 October evening and the Asian hours, then built through 12, 14 and 21 as the European drift developed before holding in the low twenties for the last three hours. Stress rose steadily from 45 to 53 inside the elevated band and Confidence stayed between 86 and 88, so the record describes a regime that has deteriorated gradually rather than abruptly. Dominant mode was trend-up through the 6 October cash session, mixed from 20:00Z onward, and trend-down for the last three hours.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to hold near 23 while the widening retracement off the session low keeps the decline from becoming a no-retracement path, then firm to 24 across the 15:00Z inflation-expectations print, where an upside surprise driving yields back toward their 5.36% high is the primary conditional path. The midday lull eases it to 23, the 17:00Z 10-year note auction lifts it to 25, and the 18:00Z FOMC minutes and the 19:00Z delayed-second-leg hour carry the highest conditional Tail at 27, so three slots reach the elevated band and the orange mapped state. The window returns to 24 into the 20:00Z cash close, then decays to 19 post-close and to a 12 to 16 overnight baseline across the Asian hours, before a measured rebuild through the European session of 8 October to 19 at the 12:30Z jobless-claims hour and 21 at the following cash open. Stress tracks the same shape between 45 and 58 without leaving the elevated band, and Confidence holds at 87 throughout.
